key_features.classic_presentation: Pyelonephritis (kidney infection) presents with FLANK PAIN (unilateral or bilateral), HIGH FEVER (>101°F) with rigors (shaking chills), and urinary symptoms. Pain is CONSTANT, ACHING, 6-8/10 severity in flank/back. Onset is within 1-3 days. Simple cystitis (bladder infection) has urinary symptoms WITHOUT fever or flank pain. Key urinary symptoms: DYSURIA (burning with urination), frequency, urgency, sometimes hematuria. Location: CVA (costovertebral angle) tenderness, lower abdominal discomfort. Key associated symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, malaise. More common in FEMALES. Key history: Prior UTIs, sexual activity, diabetes, pregnancy. Key positives: Fever + flank pain + dysuria = classic triad of pyelonephritis. CVA tenderness. Key negatives: No fever with just dysuria suggests cystitis not pyelonephritis. Unilateral flank pain without urinary symptoms more likely kidney stone.

red_flags: Sepsis (hypotension, altered mental status, high fever) - urosepsis, call 911
Pregnant patient with pyelonephritis - high risk, needs hospitalization
Diabetic with pyelonephritis - higher risk of complications
Severe nausea/vomiting with inability to tolerate oral antibiotics - needs IV antibiotics
